detect_crossings implements the D2 policy: per area and per recorded dimension it compares the LATEST sample against the mean of the trailing baseline_window PRIOR samples and flags a crossing when latest >= baseline * (1 + degradation_factor) with a positive baseline - a RELATIVE degradation against the area's OWN history, never an absolute threshold; a crossing is ADVISORY while the area has fewer than calibration_min samples. Defaults BASELINE_WINDOW=5, DEGRADATION_FACTOR=0.5, CALIBRATION_MIN=8 are the recommended D2 values, tunable per call. I reproduced independently: a rising 8-sample alpha series crosses and is TRUSTED (advisory False at >= calibration_min); a flat beta series does NOT cross (non-vacuous); a 6-sample rising series is ADVISORY True (measured, not yet trusted); flattening the latest sample back to baseline REMOVES the crossing (the recorded number drives it, not a flag); an n<2 area yields no crossing.
